title: What The Great String War relies on

entities.title: Y's design documents
entities.summary: The strings section of the Y proposal, the string ideas of earlier iterations, the constraint language's strings, and the Rust implementation of y-string, all in the padresmurfa/y repository.
entities.relevance: Part 11 says what Y kept from GString, and parts 1 and 10 what Y does differently, from these documents as they stood in November 2026.
entities.details:
- `proposal/Y-proposal.md`, § 3.3, *Strings: the y-string library*
- `proposal/Y-idea-harvest.md`, § 3.1, § 3.2, § 3.5 and § 3.7
- `proposal/constraint-language.md`
- `examples/y-string/`

The repository is private; the paths were checked to exist on its main branch on 2026-11-12.

entities.title: Voca
entities.summary: A JavaScript string library, one of the libraries whose union part 11's catalogue of methods was taken to be.
entities.relevance: Part 11's catalogue, and the verdicts in parts 2 and 3 that follow from it, assume GString had what Voca and the string libraries the series names have.

entities.title: General knowledge, checked in 2026
entities.summary: Everything in the parts that is not memory, with its sources linked in the part where it is used.
entities.relevance: Each part's opening note says which of its contents are general knowledge; the links in the part are its sources.
entities.details:
- The falsehood lists and their authors (parts 2 and 3).
- The string types of the day and their quirks: BSTR's length prefix and null as empty, TCHAR, CString's GetBuffer, strstream's freeze, Java's modified UTF-8 (part 4).
- The history of UCS-2, UCS-4, UTF-16 and UTF-8, and the byte counts of the flag of England, the family emoji and the kiss (part 5).
- Normalisation, comparison and collation; the glibc 2.28 and PostgreSQL episode; strcoll and strxfrm (part 6).
- Shlemiel the painter, ropes, V8's cons strings, SpiderMonkey's ropes, javac and JEP 280, .NET's chunked StringBuilder, Python's join, Erlang's iolists and writev (part 7).
- Java's 2012 substring change, Go, Swift's Substring, string_view and Rust's &str (part 8).
- Hash flooding in 2011, SipHash and JEP 180; Herb Sutter's 1999 measurements and the C++11 and GCC 2015 ABI change; the small string optimisation; JEP 254 and PEP 393 (part 9).
- Thompson's 1968 construction, Russ Cox's 2007 article, the Stack Overflow 2016 and Cloudflare 2019 outages, RE2, Rust's regex crate and UTS #18 (part 10).
